items.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: But like Lester Young played that thing behind Billie Holiday on the CBS special

ctx.x: Well it’s sad to say, you know what we always say, jazz is our country’s music. I’m sure you’ve heard this. But we’re low man on the totem pole. You know there’s the rock &

roll and the rap and then there’s whatever country, and that’s fine. But we get more respect, or most of the jazz players will tell you, in Europe and Japan. And I don’t understand that. I don’t understand that. Because it’s a great art to play jazz. I don’t know, you know, playing drums. And I love melodic things, and lyrical things, but doing this, I can’t play “Stardust” on the drum I don’t think. If I could I’d make a lot of money. But anyway you know what they do is they don’t respect it. They don’t respect.…

chart. Let’s try this. And we don’t play anybody else’s chart. We won’t play anybody else’s. We play what we want to play. And we have it arranged the way we want it arranged and what we want to do you see.
